Time: 2 min. Teaching intent: Open the hour and connect it to the week's decision.

Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can two files both saying 'warpage' be compared directly?
Expected answer / misconception: Only after definition, geometry, stage, and conditions match.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Peak junction temperature, average die temperature, edge warpage, and center displacement are distinct outputs. Trace the visual in order: quantity; location; stage. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A course export says 'warpage 80 µm'. Ask whether this is peak-to-valley, center-to-edge, and at which temperature before ranking candidates. Boundary: The 80 µm phrase is a synthetic ambiguity exercise.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: A course export says 'warpage 80 µm'. Ask whether this is peak-to-valley, center-to-edge, and at which temperature before ranking candidates. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. The 80 µm phrase is a synthetic ambiguity exercise.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Connect this mechanism to the worked example: A measurement after debond cannot validate a prediction after grinding; construct matched pairs before computing residuals.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: One maximum can conceal a shifted hot spot or a changed deformation mode; inspect the field and the quantity used for the decision. Trace the visual in order: field pattern; summary metric; decision. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Two synthetic layouts share the same temperature maximum but differ in where the hot spot touches the memory interface. Boundary: The two-layout comparison is synthetic teaching data.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A model output is a prediction until a suitable physical comparison or justified benchmark supports the intended use. Trace the visual in order: prediction; reference; credibility claim. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: If no physical measurement is available, label the class result 'unvalidated for this use' and propose a coupon or package test.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
